# Progress — run `agent-harness-2026-11-05` (agent-harness)

What this file is: the run's journal, newest entry first, rendered by the harness from `entries.jsonl` for Michael's phone. Each entry is one session (init, coding, verify, review, retro) with its outcome, summary and questions.

The run: phase 2 of `docs/plans/2026-11-03-test-suite-redesign.md`, spec `docs/specs/2026-11-03-resident-helper.md`, one milestone H1 (6 features). A resident helper: one warm node process per driver and per lane (`lib/helper.mjs`, started lazily as a bash coproc) answers the `.mjs` questions that `ask` in `lib/record.sh` sends it, byte for byte what the spawned script printed, with a spawn whenever the helper is off (`HARNESS_HELPER=0`), absent, busy or broken. H1-01 gives the served scripts `main(argv, io)` and `lib/cli.mjs`; H1-02 builds the helper and `ask`; H1-02b moves the call sites and proves a stub run's logs identical with the helper on and off; H1-03 cuts `treekey.mjs`'s own cost; H1-04 is the proof (two solo suites, file 13 under strace, the table in `findings-and-research/2026-11-03-resident-helper.md`); H1-05 is the review and the docs. The spec's defaults are taken and marked *default* in `journal/decisions/2026-11-03-resident-helper.md`; nothing parks. No note text changes.

How to read the feature list (`feature_list.json`): array order is priority; `after` names what a feature waits on; `passes` flips when a session's fast tier is green, and the verifier re-runs every step on the full suite before H1 merges into `main`. Steer via `INBOX.md` on this branch: line 1 `status: pause|stop`, answers under `## Answers`.

summary: All eleven served scripts export main(argv, io) → { rc, out } and share lib/cli.mjs's isMain/runCli tail; no shell file changed. 37 unit tests compare main to the CLI. Fixed a spec bug: its write-then-exit tail cuts a pipe at 64 KB, so runCli exits from the write's callback. Fast tier green.
verified_how: check.sh --fast: green, 618 tests, 158 s (the tree's cached run). 00-unit 182/182 (145 before). bash tests/run.sh 34-check-key 81-partial-key 84-node-memo 13-run-2: 129/129. node --check on every .mjs touched; the step 5 greps and step 7's git diff print nothing. The full suite was not run here: it runs at verify.

dead_ends.why: a 5 MB write to `| (sleep 0.3; wc -c)` arrived as 65536 bytes, 4 runs of 4

discoveries.text: A served main still resolves a relative path argument against the process's cwd (readFileSync(a), existsSync(b), resolve(a)); only treekey.mjs uses io.cwd by name. lib/helper.mjs must process.chdir(req.cwd) per request (requests are one at a time) or ask must spawn on a relative path, or a lane that has cd'd gets the wrong file.
helper.mjs's reply must not exit before its write's callback: on stdin EOF wait for the last write, as runCli does (a pipe write over 64 KB is async).

main's stderr is still console.error, so in the helper it lands on the helper's stderr: it stays in H1-02b's call-site table. main takes stdin only through io.stdin: readStdin throws /no stdin/ without it, so the helper's request pipe is safe and such a call comes back rc 70 unless ask spawns it first.

git spawned in needs.mjs and overlap.mjs (gitIn) inherits process.env, not io.env: all use git -C <dir>, so the cwd is safe, but a GIT_ variable set on one call would not reach them through the helper. treekey.mjs does pass io.env to its git.

A throw now exits 70 in all eleven (10 of them exited 1 uncaught). lib/record.sh:447 reads `(( $? == 1 )) || return 0` after entries.mjs validate, so a validate that throws (an unreadable entry.json) now skips the resume and goes on to the ingest. No check depends on it; H1-05 should look at that line.

tests/unit/cli-same.mjs is the shared comparison (sameAsCli, cli, mainOf, sameBytes); it swallows main's console.error. needs.mjs moves a sibling state dir's open question forward, so a test's twin state dir must not sit beside the first.

questions:
The spec's tail wrote and then exited; runCli waits for the write and treats EPIPE as no failure, and a throw's partial stdout is dropped (rc 70, no out), both marked *default*. Say in INBOX.md if you want otherwise.

dead_ends.tried: `done 2> /dev/null` on the coproc's loop that closes inherited descriptors
dead_ends.why: bash parks stderr on a high fd for that redirect, the loop closes it, and the helper loses its stderr: the throw check caught it. Closing an fd that is gone is silent, so no redirect is needed.

dead_ends.tried: the environment's names in the lock file (one file)
dead_ends.why: a refused asker's `>` open truncates it while the holder reads, which could send an empty env. They have their own file now.
a ( ) closes the coproc's fds, so every call spawned and ask looked as slow as a spawn (33 ms). Timed in the owner shell it is 3.1 ms.

dead_ends.tried: a Gotcha line for that fact
dead_ends.why: memlint: 16 lines, over 15. The section was at its limit and every other line guards a test failure, so it went; helper_ready's comment and the decision file hold it.

discoveries.text: Only the shell that sourced record.sh starts a helper, and a $( ask ) before it has one spawns and starts none. Most driver call sites are $( ), so H1-02b must call helper_start itself in run_paths or at the lane's start, outside any 2> redirect: the helper's stderr is the shell's at that moment for its whole life.

helper_start clobbers $!: coproc sets it. Today's four `$!` reads (check.sh:67, driver.sh:96 and :161, record.sh:294) are each right after their `&`, and `wait -n` in lane_wait names its pids, so none breaks; a new `$!` read must stay adjacent. No bare `wait` in lib/ or bin/ (it would wait on the coproc for ever).

A served script's stderr goes to the helper's stderr whatever the call redirects: `F x 2> /dev/null` no longer silences a throw's stack, and `2>> run.log` no longer lands there. needs.mjs fields prints NULs (the helper declines, the spawn answers): that call site stays a spawn.

ask spawns in a ( ), a pipeline's side or a job: bash closes the coproc's fds there and leaves the variables. So `ask x | y` is a spawn, and a check counting starts must not wrap ask in ( ). `export -p`-free environment enumeration is compgen -e through scratch's helper-<shell>.names.
Scratch gains helper-<shell>.lock, .names and, after a failure, .restarts. A check that lists a run's scratch directory exactly would see them once call sites ask.

A main slower than HARNESS_HELPER_TIMEOUT (120 s), a writer included, is killed and then spawned, so it can run twice: the review should look at whether any served writer can take that long (needs sweep, summary build).

proposed_changes: The spec's request line should name `env`, and `HELPER_SHELL=$BASHPID` and an `$SRANDOM` id replace its `$$` and counter: reasons in decisions/2026-11-03-resident-helper. The spec itself is left as written.
